about: Machine-readable catalog of the viz report component kit. SOURCE OF TRUTH for components. Pick by `source_shape`, copy `example_lines`, fill the slots.

rules.authoring: You write ONLY the body fragment — the <section> markup, shaped like references/body-skeleton.html. scripts/build_report.py splices it into assets/template.html. Never read or copy the template: ~25k chars of tokens, kit CSS and theme/lightbox scripts are added for you.
rules.custom_css: Report-local CSS goes in a <style> block at the top of the body fragment, under a `/* report-specific: <name> */` comment. The shared kit's <style> is in the shell's <head> and is not yours to edit. See references/custom-components.md.
rules.colour: Only design tokens (var(--accent), var(--green), ...). A literal hex anywhere outside the :root token blocks is a bug — one theme goes unreadable.
rules.javascript: Components must run with zero JS. The board renders reports in a sandboxed, script-free iframe; anything script-driven is invisible there.
rules.external_assets: No CDN, no remote fonts, no remote images. Reports must open offline from a file:// path.
rules.caption:
Every diagram or chart-like block gets a sibling

one line saying what the reader should take from it

. If the caption can't be written, delete the block.
rules.diagram_budget_note: At most 1 draw.io diagram per report - the big-picture one. A 2nd needs a separate branching flow and a stated reason (pass --diagram-budget 2 to the validator). Components are unlimited.

diagram_altitude.principle: A diagram is the big picture at product altitude - actors, concepts, outcomes in words a non-developer reads. Never the implementation with arrows.
diagram_altitude.labels:
Plain words, 5 or fewer, one line. No class, file, method, route, or table names (no SalePaymentService, no Report.jsx, no rows(), no GET /x/y, no cash_transactions). No
.
diagram_altitude.nodes: 8 or fewer. More than that is a system, not a story - split into components.
diagram_altitude.edges: Happy path only. Error, rollback, 4xx/5xx and infrastructure-failure edges belong in a sibling .callout, never in the graph. A branch is a product choice (matched / needs review), not a guard clause.
diagram_altitude.shapes: No DB cylinders, no subgraph-per-layer, no condition-from-code edge labels.
diagram_altitude.identifiers_home: Technical identifiers live in the file-touch map and breakdown cards. Put them there every time; the diagram never needs them.
diagram_altitude.validator:
scripts/diagram.py lint errors on identifiers,
, and error-path words inside labels; warns on >8 nodes and >5-word labels. Fix by rewriting the label at product altitude, not by renaming past the regex.

rules.overflow: Anything wider than the text column (tables, swimlanes, bridge charts, diagram images) goes in a container with class `card diagram` (which is overflow-x: auto), never a bare card.

all_of: the graph has a branch, a merge, a cycle, or a cross-cutting edge
the graph has 4 or more nodes
diagram_allowed_when.otherwise: Use `rail` (linear pipeline) or `chips` (2–3 ordering facts). A numbered task order is NOT evidence of dependencies.

select.source_shape: Linear pipeline, stage sequence, 'then, then, then'
Phases cascading into each other, scope narrowing
Magnitudes on one shared scale (effort, file counts)
Who does what at each stage (actor x stage)
Before/after, current/proposed, option A vs B
Risk (likelihood x impact) or effort x value quadrants
Two or three ordering facts, blockers
A matrix of facts (thing x capability, current state)
A constraint or gotcha that must not be skimmed past
Branching / merging / cyclic flow with 4+ nodes, told at product altitude (actors, outcomes) - the one big-picture diagram

primitives.purpose: Neutral surface block: token background, border, radius, padding.
Flex row (wrapping, centre-aligned) / flex column, both gap 12px.
Row with children pushed to opposite ends, wraps on narrow screens.
Two-column definition list of label/value rows that line up.

primitives.class: u-muted / u-strong / u-sm / u-label / u-num / u-scroll-x
primitives.purpose: Text + layout helpers: muted colour, semibold, 13px, uppercase micro-label, tabular numerals, horizontal scroll.
Token text colours for a single element.

components.name: Step rail
components.use_for: A linear pipeline, a stage sequence, 'then, then, then'.
components.replaces: The default replacement for an A --> B --> C flowchart.

modifiers.rail.vertical: Stacks the steps and drops the chevrons — better past ~5 steps or with long descriptions.

example_lines: Provider payload becomes a canonical row.
gotchas: Chevrons are drawn between steps and hidden below 640px, where the rail stacks.

components.name: Waterfall (staircase)
components.use_for: Phases that descend into each other, scope narrowing, a cascade where each level is a consequence of the one above.

inline_vars.--d: Indent depth, 0 1 2 3 ... — set on each .wf. Varying it IS the component.

example_lines: One class per bank, behind a shared interface.
Possible only once adapters return a stable cursor.
Reads synced rows; blocked until Phase 2 lands.
gotchas: Indent collapses to 0 below 640px so nothing overflows on mobile.

components.name: Waterfall (bridge bars)
components.use_for: The finance-style waterfall: a starting value, +/- deltas, a resulting total. Also budget or effort deltas between plan revisions.

inline_vars.bottom: Where the bar floats, % of the plot.
inline_vars.height: The bar's magnitude, % of the plot.

gotchas: Pick a scale first (above: 42k = 60%, so ~0.7k per point), then carry the running total forward: each bar's bottom is the previous bar's bottom+height.
A `down` bar starts where the previous ended and drops by its own height, so its bottom is prev_top minus height.
Totals sit on the baseline (bottom:0); only deltas float.

components.name: Proportion bars
components.use_for: Magnitudes that share a scale — effort per phase, files per layer, test counts. Cheaper to read than a pie or a bar chart.

inline_vars.width: Fill width as a % of the track.

gotchas: Widths are percentages of the widest value, not of a total — keep one scale across all rows.

components.name: Swimlane
components.use_for: Who does what at each stage (actor x stage).
components.replaces: A Mermaid flowchart full of subgraphs.

inline_vars.--cols: Number of stage columns (excludes the lane-label column).

modifiers.cell.empty: Dashed, faded — this actor does nothing at this stage.

gotchas: Cells are laid out in reading order — emit exactly --cols cells after every .lane, including empties.

components.name: Layer stack
components.use_for: Architecture drawn as tiers (UI -> API -> service -> store).
components.replaces: The 'boxes stacked vertically' flowchart. This is the default for the Architecture section.
example_lines: Cash-flow page, React Query services triad
gotchas: The arrow is drawn in the gap under each band except the last — don't add your own.

components.name: Stat tiles
components.use_for: The counts a reader wants before reading anything — phases, tasks, files, endpoints, estimated hours.
gotchas: Only counts that exist in the source. Never derive an impressive-looking number the plan doesn't state.

components.name: Compare
components.container: none — .side elements carry their own card
components.use_for: Before/after, current/proposed, option A vs option B.
gotchas: Collapses to one column below 720px, so put the 'before' side first.

components.name: Matrix (2x2)
components.use_for: Quadrants — risk (likelihood x impact), effort x value.
example_lines:
Mitigate first

  • Duplicate rows on retry

Plan for

  • Bank revokes the API key
gotchas: Emit exactly: corner, 2 axis labels, then per row one .ax.y and two .q — the grid has no auto-placement slack.

components.name: Timeline
components.use_for: Dated milestones or a rollout order. Use instead of a Gantt whenever there are no real durations.
gotchas: Dates in the document's own format — never invent one that isn't in the source.

components.name: Dependency chips
components.use_for: Two or three ordering facts, blockers.
components.replaces: Every trivial dependency flowchart. Fan-out reads fine: one chip, arrow, several chips, arrow.
gotchas: Chips between two arrows are understood as running in parallel — don't put a strict order there.

components.name: Status table
components.use_for: A matrix of facts — integration x capability, module x state. Pair with tag chips so gaps are scannable.
gotchas: Wrap in `card diagram` — wide tables must scroll inside the card, not stretch the page.

components.name: Callout
components.container: none — it is its own block
components.use_for: A constraint or gotcha that must not be skimmed past.
example_lines: MySQL caps index names at 64 chars — SQLite won't catch it in tests.
gotchas: Three or four per report at most; past that nothing stands out.

components.name: Legend
components.container: inside the diagram's card, after the visual
components.use_for: Under any diagram whose colours carry meaning.
gotchas: Only add one where colour actually varies — a legend for a single-colour diagram is noise.

components.name: Tag + caption
components.use_for: `.tag` qualifies a heading inline; `.cap` is the one-line takeaway under a diagram.
example_lines: Every provider path converges on the same dedup gate.
gotchas: Every diagram gets a .cap — if the takeaway can't be written, the diagram isn't earning its place.

components.name: draw.io diagram
components.use_for: The one big-picture graph per report: a flow that branches, merges, or cycles, 4-8 nodes, plain words at product altitude. Built with scripts/diagram.py (DIAGRAM.md), embedded as its .drawio.png.

slots.img: src = relative path to docs/diagrams/<topic>/<name>.drawio.png, alt = the caption
slots.p.cap: required takeaway line (same text as the .mmd caption)

example_lines: Every payment ends in one cash report.
gotchas: Build the diagram first (DIAGRAM.md); never write <pre class="mermaid"> in a report.
The PNG keeps a white canvas in dark theme - that is expected.
Click opens the lightbox automatically; do not add handlers.
